exposure: Treatment group (UDCA alone vs. UDCA plus SAMe)
Treatment with ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) alone vs. UDCA plus S-adenosyl methionine (SAMe)
outcome: Pathological placental findings (maternal malperfusion, pathological fetal vascular supply, inflammatory lesions)
cohort: 89 pregnancies complicated by mICP (defined as total serum bile acids (TSBAs) levels <40 µmol/L)
finding: The study found no significant differences in APO rates or placental histopathology between pregnancies complicated by mICP managed with UDCA alone compared to those treated with UDCA plus SAMe.
mod_finding: While there were no significant differences in cesarean section rates between the two treatment groups, instrumental vaginal delivery was more common in the UDCA plus SAMe group.
